tb21_profile.skill: Compile an arithmetic algorithm (isqrt then Fibonacci mod 2^32) down to a machine with only NOT/AND/OR/XOR over single bits: build adders, comparators and muxes, sequence them as state over simulation steps, and fit inside a line/step budget
tb21_profile.domain: Digital logic / gate-level netlists and bit-level 32-bit arithmetic, driven by a small custom simulator whose semantics must be read out of sim.c
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec for a restricted target machine, with a hard size budget - almost certainly by writing a generator program that emits the netlist

TMax-15K.reason: Translate a high-level instruction list into the exact binary encoding a small machine executes, then emulate it - authoring a program for a restricted target.
Recover a stack machine's instruction semantics by experimenting with the binary, then reimplement it exactly - the read-sim.c-carefully skill.
Implement a bytecode VM in C from a written opcode spec; precise, unforgiving machine semantics with no library to lean on.
Build a custom bytecode emulator from its specification; same low-level execution-model reasoning, in Python.
Stack-based expression VM in C that must evaluate correctly once built - operand ordering and state at the machine level.
Broken stack-VM C project must be made to build and execute programs correctly; debugging an interpreter's core loop.
Finish a DSP bytecode emulator in C - instruction decode and per-step state update, like the simulator's step loop.
Implement a service around a specified assembly instruction set; must honour an instruction semantics table exactly.
Port an interpreter that parses a simple instruction set and computes a result; small-machine semantics preserved across a rewrite.
Port a mathematical checksum virtual machine, keeping its bit-exact arithmetic behaviour in a minimal container.

Sort data in memory in ARM64 assembly - nested loops and comparisons written out by hand.
Read a limit and compute over a loop in ARM64 using only syscalls; no runtime, so every step is explicit.
A generator that is supposed to satisfy the Fibonacci recurrence produces wrong values; fix the recurrence and its seeding.
Compute GCD for configured integer pairs and write exact results; the algorithm matters but the language does all the work.
Square roots of 0-9 printed in an exact format; shares the arithmetic subject but none of the low-level difficulty.

Symbolic execution over all paths of a binary - reasoning about a machine's semantics rather than running one input.

Generated code is wrong for a specific construct; debugging a code generator by reading its output, like inspecting emitted gates.
Boolean short-circuit semantics in a template interpreter - exactly the evaluation-order semantics of a boolean expression engine.
A gate-direction transformation pass rejects valid circuits; rewriting a circuit while preserving its function.
Gate synthesis plugin selection fails silently; synthesising an operation out of available primitive gates.
Implement a new gate primitive against the library's existing gate conventions - building a primitive operation correctly.
An instruction mishandles its operand set; wiring operands to a gate correctly, but a narrow API fix.
Numeric formatting of arbitrary-precision values diverges from the spec; exact-output discipline, no circuit content.

Standalone ARM64 Fibonacci with syscalls only and an exact required output format; no runtime to hide behind.
Compile a sequence of operations into the exact encoding a small machine runs, then emulate it to predict the result.
Gate operations sharing a bit get reordered and change the answer - the data-dependency hazard that dominates netlist design.
GCD in ARM64 assembly: an iterative numeric algorithm expressed purely as compares, branches and subtractions.
Work out an undocumented machine's instruction semantics by experiment, then reproduce them exactly - what reading sim.c demands.
Implement a bytecode machine in C straight from an opcode spec, with no tolerance for semantic drift.
LCM in AArch64 assembly: compose GCD, multiplication and division from instruction-level primitives.
Integer-to-decimal conversion in Gforth - repeated division and digit assembly on a machine with only a stack.

notes: Nothing in the pool is gate-level: searches for netlist, verilog, full adder, truth table and flip-flop returned nothing but quantum circuits. The nearest real transfer is (a) implementing arithmetic algorithms with only machine primitives, and (b) targeting or reverse-engineering a small custom machine. TerminalWorld and RTS turned out strongest because of the Forth isqrt seed (tw_621404, literally integer sqrt by Newton's method on a stack machine) and the large ARM64-assembly family (Fibonacci, GCD, LCM, primality), which the lexical retriever surfaced only partially - I found most of the assembly ones by searching. TMax contributes its bytecode-VM family: authoring a program for a restricted machine and recovering an undocumented machine's semantics. SWE-Rebench's qiskit cluster is the only place in the pool where someone reasons about ordering and synthesis in a gate circuit, so despite being quantum it beats the Python bugfixes; SWE-Smith is the weakest corpus here, offering only bit-packing (cantools, pyasn1, qrcode) and state-machine/codegen analogues, honest 2-3s.
